title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page, §2 'Familles de classes de cycles mod équivalence d'Albanese'): X^n and Y^m are smooth projective varieties over an algebraically closed field k. A_alb denotes cycles modulo Albanese equivalence, so that the degree-0 part of A_{0,alb}(Y) is identified via the Albanese sum map S_Y with A_Y(k), where A_Y = Alb(Y). A correspondence Z ∈ A^i_alb(X×Y) acts on 0-cycles, giving a group homomorphism u_Z : A_Y(k) → A^i_alb(X) with Z(v) = u_Z(S_Y(v)).

This page states and starts proving Theorem 2.1(ii). The claim is that u_Z is 'algebraic up to isogeny'. Precisely, there exist an isogeny of abelian varieties ('isogénie de VA') φ : A' → A_Y and a cycle Z' ∈ A^i_alb(X×A') with the following properties:
- Z'(0) = 0, where the marginal note explains that 0 means the divisor of degree 1 concentrated at the origin.
- Equivalently, a' ↦ Z'(a') is a group homomorphism v_{Z'} : A'(k) → A^i_alb(X).
- u_Z ∘ φ(k) = v_{Z'}.

Proof sketch, first in an ideal case. Suppose there is a family of 0-cycles U on Y×A_Y (codimension m) with S_Y(U(a)) = a for all a. Set Z'(a) := Z(U(a)), i.e. Z' = Z∘U as a composed correspondence. For any degree-0 cycle v, U(S(v)) and v have the same Albanese image, hence are Albanese-equivalent. Therefore Z(v) = Z'(S(v)), checked first on the cycles U(a): Z(U(a)) = Z'(S(U(a))) = Z'(a), 'O.K.'. This case would allow φ = id.

The page ends: 'Mais on ne sait pas si on peut [trouver U]'. The next page supplies the fix. One can find U with S_Y(U(a)) = n·a, for instance from a curve in Y whose Jacobian maps onto Alb(Y). One then gets Z'(S_Y(v)) = n·Z(v), and uses divisibility of A_Y(k) to get rid of the factor n, which is where the isogeny comes in.

Purpose: to show that correspondences act on Albanese-equivalence classes of 0-cycles through morphisms of abelian varieties, up to isogeny. This is part of a systematic treatment of 'algebraic families' of cycle classes, in the setting of the standard conjectures and Hodge/Tate/Lefschetz-type questions.
errors: Z(v) = Z'(S(v)) for degree-0 v needs the cycles U(a) to be of degree 0, or else normalized as U(a) − U(0). Otherwise v and U(S(v)) need not be Albanese-equivalent. The normalization Z'(0)=0 (replace Z' by Z' − pr_X^*Z'(0)) plays this role, but it is only implicit here.
Equating 'Z'(0)=0' with 'a' ↦ Z'(a) is a homomorphism' needs justification: the map factors through an abelian variety (theorem of the cube / rigidity). This is only asserted.
The ideal case assumes the existence of U with S_Y∘U = id, which Grothendieck himself immediately notes is not known. The real proof is on the next page.

ideas.what: 0-cycles of degree 0 modulo Albanese equivalence identified with Alb_Y(k) via the sum map S_Y
A correspondence Z acting on Alb_Y(k) is induced, up to an isogeny, by an algebraic family Z' on X×A' that is additive (Z'(0)=0)
ideas.modern_name: regular homomorphisms / algebraic representatives; action of correspondences on Albanese via composition with a family of 0-cycles

ideas.what: Constructing a family of 0-cycles U with S_Y(U(a)) = n·a, then using divisibility of A_Y(k) to remove n
ideas.modern_name: standard surjectivity of Jacobians of curves onto Albanese; divisibility trick

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working-out of the functoriality of Albanese-equivalence classes of 0-cycles under correspondences, up to isogeny. It is classical (Weil, Samuel, later Murre) and the argument is the standard one. Nothing here appears new.
transcription_corrections: First line 'de UA' should read 'de VA' (variétés abéliennes), continuing 'isogénie de VA' from the previous page.
The subscript is 'alb' (Albanese equivalence), not 'alg': A^i_alb(X × A'), A^i_alb(X), A_{0 alb}(Y).
The struck symbol in Z' ∈ A^i_alb(X × A') is a correction of the X itself. The intended factor is most likely X, not X'.
The marginal note under Z'(0) reads roughly '(0) = diviseur de degré 1 concentré en 0'. The following phrase is 'ou, ce qui revient au même, tel que'.
'l'application v_{Z'} : a' ↦ Z'(a') de A'(k) dans A^i_alb(X)' (the deleted word is likely 'A'(k)').
